summary: Helen Moore Johnson was an Indologist who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1912 and studied under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins University. She taught at Oxford College for Women and held a post at Johns Hopkins (1924–1936).

Helen Wang specializes in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London (~1984–1988) and became Curator of East Asian Money in the British Museum's Department of Coins and Medals around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (both attested in 1999).
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1979 to 1984. She held an academic post at Rice University around 1990.

Helena Willman-Grabowska was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After earning her Dr. ès lettres at the University of Paris, she taught at Paris, the EPHE, and as a professor at Jagiellonian University (1927–1948).

Helga Uebach worked in Tibetology and Indology, completing her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (~1961–1967) under Helmut Hoffmann. In 1964, she served as an editorial consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Hellfried Dahlmann was a scholar of linguistics who held academic appointments at the University of Marburg (~1935–1944) and the University of Cologne (~1951–1970).

Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm earned his doctorate under Otto Franke at Berlin (~1928–1932). He founded the Deutschland-Institut Peking, taught German at Peking University (~1933–1948), and held the chair of Sinology at the University of Washington (1948–1971).

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (Ph.D. ~1945–1948) and under Paul Debes. He later served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from circa 1953 to 1988.

Helmer Smith was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied at Uppsala University and under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, Dines Andersen, and others. He served as docent at Lund University and later professor at Uppsala University (1936–1947).
Helmut Arntz was a linguist who studied under Hermann Hirt from circa 1931 to 1934. He held an academic post at the University of Giessen from circa 1935 to 1945.

Helmut Eimer, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Berlin, Hamburg, and the University of Bonn, completing his Promotion under Frank-Richard Hamm in 1974. He subsequently held a post at the University of Bonn (~1974–2001).

Helmut Hoffmann was an Indologist and Tibetologist who earned his Dr. phil. at Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. He served as professor of Indology and Iranistics at Munich (1948–1968) and later as professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, completed his doctorate under Ernst Steinkellner and his habilitation at the University of Vienna. He taught at Vienna and directed the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (2007–2014).

Helmut Nespital specialized in Indology and linguistics, earning a Ph.D. under Vincenc Pořízka at Charles University and his habilitation at Berlin. He taught at Humboldt University, the University of Bamberg, and as Professor of Indology at Freie Universität Berlin.

Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Karl Hoffmann and completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg. After his habilitation at Tübingen, he served as professor at the University of Regensburg (1966–1982) and the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Steinkellner, receiving his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna in 1981. He served as assistant and associate professor at Vienna from 1981 to 2015.

Helmut Uhlig, a scholar of Buddhist studies and archaeology, studied at the University of Vienna (~1941–1944). He worked as a teacher at the Volkshochschule and became director of Volkshochschule Tempelhof in 1956.

Helmuth Peter Holler, active in religious studies and Indology, studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and Kiel University. He served as principal of Rajahmundry Seminary (1897–1900) and founded and served as professor and principal at Oriental University (~1903–1925).

Helmuth von Glasenapp was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. under Hermann Jacobi at Bonn. He served as professor at the University of Königsberg (1928–1944) and the University of Tübingen (1946–1959).
